# Network Operations

This is the authoritative documentation for the current network state.

## Settled Design (2026-10-19)
**Architecture:** One two-way WARP tunnel (`wgcf-ingress`) from the decoy to the host.
- **Tunnel Characteristics:**
  - Decoy terminates WireGuard (`wg-opdbus`, 10.0.0.1).
  - Decoy seals peer identity (OIA1).
  - fwmark selects `wgcf-ingress` for egress.
  - a simple plain TCP port (8090) is the target.
- **Addressing:**
  - Public host addressing: `pub0`.
  - Internal fabric: `ovsbr0` retains OpenFlow `10.200.0.1`.
- **Decoy Routing:**
  - Administrative SSH (TCP 22/2222) is DNAT'd from `10.0.0.1` to `188.68.58.237:22` via table `ip wgcf_admin_ssh`.
- **SOP:** No inner tunnels (GRE, SSH TUN, MASQUE, Xray) are required or active.

#    and restores affected consumers' wanted states. Only active + previous remain.
#
# Undo the last release:
#   sudo /usr/local/libexec/opdbus-release/op-release-launch rollback
set -eu
PATH=/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin
LC_ALL=C
export PATH LC_ALL

REPO=$(CDPATH= cd -- "$(dirname -- "$(readlink -f "$0")")" && pwd)
OP_RELEASE_DIR=$(realpath -e -- "${OP_RELEASE_DIR:-"$REPO/target/release"}")
export OP_RELEASE_DIR
RELEASE_BASE=/usr/local/libexec/opdbus-release
RELEASE_LAUNCH=$RELEASE_BASE/op-release-launch
RELEASE_BIN=$RELEASE_BASE/op-release
RELEASE_BOOT=/etc/init.d/op-release-activate

[ "$(id -u)" = 0 ] || { echo 'activate-golden.sh: run as root (sudo ./activate-golden.sh)' >&2; exit 1; }
[ "$#" = 0 ] || { echo 'activate-golden.sh: takes no arguments' >&2; exit 1; }
# Check the execution path before invoking any installed kit code. The launcher
# independently checks the complete approved manifest and kernel/BTF pair.
for directory in / /usr /usr/local /usr/local/libexec "$RELEASE_BASE" /etc /etc/init.d; do
    directory_mode=0$(stat -c %a "$directory")
    [ -d "$directory" ] && [ ! -L "$directory" ] &&
        [ "$(stat -c %u:%g "$directory")" = 0:0 ] &&
        [ "$((directory_mode & 07022))" -eq 0 ] ||
        { echo "activate-golden.sh: insecure release-kit directory: $directory" >&2; exit 1; }
done
for artifact in "$RELEASE_LAUNCH" "$RELEASE_BIN" "$RELEASE_BOOT"; do
    [ -f "$artifact" ] && [ ! -L "$artifact" ] &&
        [ "$(stat -c %u:%g:%a:%h "$artifact")" = 0:0:755:1 ] ||
        { echo "activate-golden.sh: install the approved root-owned release kit: $artifact" >&2; exit 1; }
done
cmp -s "$RELEASE_LAUNCH" "$REPO/deploy/release/op-release-launch" &&
    cmp -s "$RELEASE_BIN" "$OP_RELEASE_DIR/op-release" &&
    cmp -s "$RELEASE_BOOT" "$REPO/deploy/release/op-release-activate" ||
    { echo 'activate-golden.sh: installed release kit differs from this build; refusing an old or mixed kit' >&2; exit 1; }

"$RELEASE_LAUNCH" provision-slots
"$REPO/deploy/lib/golden/build-golden.sh"
exec "$RELEASE_LAUNCH" release

#!/bin/sh
# activate-golden.sh — the one command for deploying a new version.
#
#   sudo ./activate-golden.sh
#
# Run it after the release build and seal:
#   CXXFLAGS="-include cstdint" cargo build --workspace --release
#   sudo target/release/opblob seal-shm && sudo target/release/opblob persist
# OP_RELEASE_DIR selects one prepared optimized artifact directory for both
# release-controller verification and golden preparation (default target/release).
#
# What it does:
# 1. Native provision-slots reconciles any interrupted transaction and prepares
#    the owned golden/slot layout. Recovery-only work stops this invocation.
# 2. Prepares /opt/op-dbus/golden from target/release and the sealed catalog
#    (internal helper deploy/lib/golden/build-golden.sh; it never builds or seals).
# 3. Native release sends/receives the immutable generation into the inactive
#    slot, rotates read-only overlays at the inventory's owned host targets,
#    and restores affected consumers' wanted states. Only active + previous remain.
#
# Undo the last release:
#   sudo /usr/local/libexec/opdbus-release/op-release-launch rollback
set -eu
PATH=/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin
LC_ALL=C
export PATH LC_ALL

REPO=$(CDPATH= cd -- "$(dirname -- "$(readlink -f "$0")")" && pwd)
OP_RELEASE_DIR=$(realpath -e -- "${OP_RELEASE_DIR:-"$REPO/target/release"}")
export OP_RELEASE_DIR
RELEASE_BASE=/usr/local/libexec/opdbus-release
RELEASE_LAUNCH=$RELEASE_BASE/op-release-launch
RELEASE_BIN=$RELEASE_BASE/op-release
RELEASE_BOOT=/etc/init.d/op-release-activate

[ "$(id -u)" = 0 ] || { echo 'activate-golden.sh: run as root (sudo ./activate-golden.sh)' >&2; exit 1; }
[ "$#" = 0 ] || { echo 'activate-golden.sh: takes no arguments' >&2; exit 1; }
# Check the execution path before invoking any installed kit code. The launcher
# independently checks the complete approved manifest and kernel/BTF pair.
for directory in / /usr /usr/local /usr/local/libexec "$RELEASE_BASE" /etc /etc/init.d; do
    directory_mode=0$(stat -c %a "$directory")
    [ -d "$directory" ] && [ ! -L "$directory" ] &&
        [ "$(stat -c %u:%g "$directory")" = 0:0 ] &&
        [ "$((directory_mode & 07022))" -eq 0 ] ||
        { echo "activate-golden.sh: insecure release-kit directory: $directory" >&2; exit 1; }
done
for artifact in "$RELEASE_LAUNCH" "$RELEASE_BIN" "$RELEASE_BOOT"; do
    [ -f "$artifact" ] && [ ! -L "$artifact" ] &&
        [ "$(stat -c %u:%g:%a:%h "$artifact")" = 0:0:755:1 ] ||
        { echo "activate-golden.sh: install the approved root-owned release kit: $artifact" >&2; exit 1; }
done
cmp -s "$RELEASE_LAUNCH" "$REPO/deploy/release/op-release-launch" &&
    cmp -s "$RELEASE_BIN" "$OP_RELEASE_DIR/op-release" &&
    cmp -s "$RELEASE_BOOT" "$REPO/deploy/release/op-release-activate" ||
    { echo 'activate-golden.sh: installed release kit differs from this build; refusing an old or mixed kit' >&2; exit 1; }

"$RELEASE_LAUNCH" provision-slots
"$REPO/deploy/lib/golden/build-golden.sh"
exec "$RELEASE_LAUNCH" release

content.text:
[crates/op-deployment/src/bin/release/lifetime.rs#8563]
1://! Adapter for the pinned downstream Btrfs quiescent-destroy ABI.
2://! No userspace scan, kernel-version guess, or ordinary-delete fallback is safe.
3:use std::{io, os::fd::{AsRawFd, BorrowedFd}};
4:use uuid::Uuid;
5:
6:// deploy/release/lifetime/0001-btrfs-quiescent-destroy.patch, native Linux ABI:
7:// _IOW(BTRFS_IOCTL_MAGIC /* 0x94 */, 255, struct ... /* 96 bytes */).
8:const SNAP_DESTROY_QUIESCENT: libc::c_ulong = 0x4060_94ff;
9:
10:#[repr(C)]
11:struct QuiescentDestroy {
12:    subvolid: u64,
13:    fsid: [u8; 16],
14:    uuid: [u8; 16],
15:    received_uuid: [u8; 16],
16:    flags: u64,
17:    reserved: [u64; 4],
18:}
19:const _: () = assert!(std::mem::size_of::<QuiescentDestroy>() == 96);
20:
21:// The caller journals exact identity before this call and must close its own
22:// target-root descriptors/mounts first. `top` is a different root on the same
23:// filesystem. Source snapshots and aborted incoming roots use this same path;
24:// they must be read-only too (a zero received UUID is valid).
25://
26:// The kernel holds admission closed continuously from its reference census
27:// through unlink. Success permanently closes the old incarnation; no userspace
28:// lease/Drop unlock is needed while the caller waits for the cleaner and renames
29:// the incoming root. Live-alias rejection precedes root unlink. Other failures
30:// can follow unlink, so recovery must reconcile identity after every error.
31:// The ABI reserves EBUSY/ESTALE/EROFS/EINVAL for pre-unlink rejection and maps
32:// all failures after root unlink starts to EIO. EIO never promises rollback.
33:// ENOENT is special to this checked ABI: its kernel lifetime registry includes
34:// orphan root objects through final free and proves the exact generation has
35:// no live inode aliases. Pathname absence or native cleaner completion alone
36:// never substitutes for that proof. A busy orphan remains admission-closed.
37:// ENOTTY means the required kernel is absent and must remain a hard failure.
38:pub fn destroy(
39:    top: BorrowedFd<'_>,
40:    fsid: Uuid,
41:    subvolid: u64,
42:    native_uuid: Uuid,
43:    received_uuid: Uuid,
44:) -> io::Result<()> {
45:    let args = QuiescentDestroy {
46:        subvolid,
47:        fsid: fsid.into_bytes(),
48:        uuid: native_uuid.into_bytes(),
49:        received_uuid: received_uuid.into_bytes(),
50:        flags: 0,
51:        reserved: [0; 4],
52:    };
53:    // SAFETY: the fixed-layout, fully initialized 96-byte input and borrowed
54:    // ioctl-capable directory descriptor remain valid throughout the syscall.
55:    let result = unsafe { libc::ioctl(top.as_raw_fd(), SNAP_DESTROY_QUIESCENT, &args) };
56:    match result {
57:        0 => Ok(()),
58:        -1 => Err(io::Error::last_os_error()),
59:        _ => Err(io::Error::from_raw_os_error(libc::EPROTO)),
60:    }
61:}

content.thinking: Mapping EBUSY failure paths for quiescent-destroy and analyzing LIFETIME_READY state for an old root.

content.text:
Found the actual EBUSY map — and the limit of what I can see from userspace. The custom kernel patch returns `EBUSY` in exactly four spots, all inside the kernel's root-lifetime registry:

1. Someone holds the root's quiesce semaphore (a stuck concurrent destroy — e.g., the Oct-29 failure itself).
2. **The root object exists but was never marked `LIFETIME_READY`** — "root-item identity is not stable until canonical publication." For a superseded slot root, this is the prime suspect.
3. Semaphore contention at the orphan-close step.
4. Live inodes surviving dentry prune — but my full `/proc` scan found **zero** userspace holders, and swap is a partition, so this one points back at (1)/(2): kernel-side state, not a process.

Which of the four fires is unobservable without kernel tracing (`ftrace` on the btrfs functions or inspecting the BPF guard state) — that's host-kernel instrumentation, and I'm not doing it unilaterally.

Recorded in HANDOFF/SIGNALS as the precise gate. Your calls stack up as: **deploy path** (blocked on this EBUSY — options are the ftrace probe, the Oct-22 FUSE/cf-mesh refresh, or hold), **web3** (needs the on-stage decision), **2a/2b**, **bridge restriction**. The release build, seal, golden, and UI work are all staged and verified behind those decisions.

No — rescue env is the most expensive option and the least informative. Direct answer:

**Against it:**
- A reboot stops everything: bridge, op-web, WARP, both FUSE views, the containers, and this session's backend. Three days from submission, that's the biggest disruption on the board.
- It wouldn't diagnose anything — it would just force-delete `489` by other means, destroying the evidence of *why* the kernel holds it busy, and it bypasses the exact-generation safety the ABI exists for.
- The rescue kernel likely lacks the custom quiescent patch, so the launcher couldn't verify the delete anyway — we'd trade a stuck journal for a state/reality mismatch in `slots.json` that then needs its own reconciliation.

**What I'd do instead, in order:**
1. Check whether `crash`/`drgn` exist here for a read-only look at `489`'s quiesce semaphore and `QUIESCING` bit — that distinguishes "stuck lock from the Oct-29 failure" from "genuinely live inodes" without touching anything.
2. If the tools aren't there: the Oct-22 FUSE-refresh + `cf-mesh` restart (precedent-backed, no reboot).
3. Rescue env stays the last resort, only if 1 and 2 both fail to explain or clear it.

Want me to run the tool-availability check now?

# AI SDK

The AI layer for building frameworks and agents on Vercel

A unified TypeScript SDK for building AI apps with modern streaming, multi-model, and provider-agnostic capabilities

## Get started

Install the SDK:

```sh
npm i ai
```

- [Read the AI SDK documentation](https://ai-sdk.dev/)
- [Use AI Gateway](https://vercel.com/ai-gateway)

## Core capabilities

- **Multi-provider support:** Switch providers with one line of code.
- **Streaming that just works:** Real-time responses without custom parsing.
- **Built-in fallbacks:** Reliable production behavior by default.
- **AI Gateway compatible:** Route to any model through one endpoint.

## Example: generate text

This example sends a prompt through AI Gateway. Replace the model ID or provider configuration for your use case.

```ts
import { generateText } from 'ai';

const { text } = await generateText({
  model: 'openai/gpt-5',
  prompt: 'Explain the concept of quantum entanglement.',
});

console.log(text);
```

## Scale with confidence

Plug the AI SDK into an entire ecosystem designed for modern AI applications that scale.

### [Vercel AI Gateway](https://vercel.com/ai-gateway)
Access 400+ models with no markup or having to manage multiple API keys.

### [Vercel Sandbox](https://vercel.com/sandbox)
Run agent generated code securely and at scale.

### [Workflows](https://vercel.com/workflows)
Build long-running AI agents and apps that can suspend, resume, and survive function timeouts.

### [AI Elements](https://elements.ai-sdk.dev/)
A UI component library and custom registry built to build AI-native applications faster.

## The framework agnostic AI toolkit

Use AI SDK with Next.js, React, Svelte, Angular, Vue, Nuxt, and Solid.

## Build with the AI SDK today

- [Chatbot Starter Template](https://vercel.com/templates/next.js/chatbot): Learn how to build a full-featured AI chatbot with persistence, multi-modal chat, and more.
- [Build a Slackbot Agent](https://vercel.com/templates/other/ai-sdk-slackbot): Learn how to build a Slackbot that responds to direct messages and mentions in channels.
- [Build a SQL Agent](https://vercel.com/templates/next.js/natural-language-postgres): Learn how to build an app that interacts with a PostgreSQL database using natural language.
- [Browse AI SDK documentation](https://ai-sdk.dev/)
- [Browse AI SDK templates](https://vercel.com/templates?type=ai)

If you encounter incorrect information, can’t find what you need, need a capability Vercel doesn’t currently offer, or have any other feedback to report, please do it by following the instructions at https://vercel.com/feedback.md.

content.thinking: Explaining why MAC addresses are an insecure trust anchor for authentication and suggesting a sound alternative.

content.text:
No — and it's important to see why, because it would give false trust while fixing nothing:

1. **Your laptop's MAC never arrives.** MACs are layer-2 — they're stripped at the first hop (your wireless router). By the time traffic traverses the WireGuard tunnel to the decoy or host, there is no laptop MAC left to log; at best you'd see the router's interface MAC, which identifies the router, not you.
2. **MACs are forgeable in seconds.** Anyone on the LAN can clone any MAC. Basing admission on it would let any neighbor in while looking secure — worse than no check, because we'd stop checking the real one.
3. **You already have the sound anchor: the WireGuard key.** The whole design mints identity from the kernel-verified tunnel peer — cryptographic, not spoofable, and the router already holds your human key. That's the path to fix: making the OIA1 pickup succeed for that key, not adding a weaker signal next to it.

If the goal is "this laptop should just work," the honest version is binding its browser session to the existing human key — want me to trace exactly where that pickup breaks for your setup?

summary.text: Explaining why MAC addresses are an insecure trust anchor for authentication and suggesting a sound alternative.

content.text:
No — and it's important to see why, because it would give false trust while fixing nothing:

1. **Your laptop's MAC never arrives.** MACs are layer-2 — they're stripped at the first hop (your wireless router). By the time traffic traverses the WireGuard tunnel to the decoy or host, there is no laptop MAC left to log; at best you'd see the router's interface MAC, which identifies the router, not you.
2. **MACs are forgeable in seconds.** Anyone on the LAN can clone any MAC. Basing admission on it would let any neighbor in while looking secure — worse than no check, because we'd stop checking the real one.
3. **You already have the sound anchor: the WireGuard key.** The whole design mints identity from the kernel-verified tunnel peer — cryptographic, not spoofable, and the router already holds your human key. That's the path to fix: making the OIA1 pickup succeed for that key, not adding a weaker signal next to it.

If the goal is "this laptop should just work," the honest version is binding its browser session to the existing human key — want me to trace exactly where that pickup breaks for your setup?

Experiment green, end to end — and I'll tell you exactly what it does and doesn't prove:

**Proven (local chain, throwaway keys, `/tmp/anchor-exp` scratch — nothing in the repos, no mainnet, no plugin or grant wiring):**
- 3 chained `etched.index-entry/1` leaves (canonical JSON → sha256 chain, matching the repo's schema).
- `keccak256` Merkle root over the leaf digests.
- `EtchedAnchor` compiles, deploys, `anchor(root)` mines (block 2), emits `Anchored(root, timestamp, label)`.
- `lookup(root)` returns exists/block/timestamp; unknown roots return false. No hallucinated state — every claim verified on-chain in the run receipt.

**Explicitly not done:** no testnet, no real key (ganache prefunded throwaway only — never touched an identity key), no `web3` plugin method, no grants, no demo wiring. content.text:
Yes — promising, with the emphasis in the right place. What the experiment actually de-risked:

- **The trust loop is complete in miniature:** operation receipt → chained canonical entry → Merkle root → on-chain record → independent lookup. Nothing in that chain is hand-waved; the receipt's `operation_id`/`event_hash` fields already exist in the repo schema, so real entries can flow into it without redesign.
- **Base Sepolia is the natural next rung:** the contract is plain EVM, no special precompiles, deploys as-is. Testnet faucet funds are free and the footprint is disposable.

What it did *not* prove (so we don't oversell it): a testnet deploy proves deployment, not the product. The demo value is the full receipt chain from a *real* operation, and that needs the plugin MethodDecl + grants + reseal — the wiring your staging doc currently keeps off the demo.

Concrete next rung if you want it: deploy this exact contract to Base Sepolia with a fresh throwaway key (faucet-funded, never an identity key), anchor one real-shaped root, and read it back from a second machine. Reversible, costs nothing, and it turns "works locally" into "works on Base." Say the word and I'll run it.

content.thinking: Assessing web3 adoption gaps and providing an honest opinion on verifiable receipts as a wedge.

content.text:
Yes — but let's name the gap precisely, because the vague version ("web3 adoption") leads to token thinking, and the precise version is your wedge:

**The actual gap is verifiable agency.** Every agent framework ships the same hole: the agent says it did X, and your only evidence is its own transcript. An auditor — or a customer in a regulated business — can't accept that. A sealed receipt chain (capability-checked at admission, committed to the event ledger) plus an on-chain anchor (existence + timestamp no one can backdate) is a complete answer to "prove what the agent did." Nobody else in the agent space has that story; they have logs.

**Two honest caveats, because a judge will raise them:**
1. Anchoring proves *existence at a time*, not truth. Garbage in, garbage anchored. Your real trust root isn't the chain — it's the admission gate (capabilities, grants, identity-bound calls). The chain is just the witness that can't be bribed. Lead with the gate, mention the chain second. That's also exactly what your own review already concluded: sell verifiability and compliance, present the blockchain as the neutral witness, never the product.
2. The UX gap you already dodge by design: no wallets, no signatures, no gas — the identity *is* the key and the user never touches one. Most "web3 adoption" friction is wallet UX; you sidestep it entirely. Don't give that away by adding wallet steps later.

So yes: big, real gap, and you're standing in it with the two halves (admission + witness) that everyone else is missing one of.

content.thinking: Clarifying that the identity key only covers admission and that chain writes require a separately bound secp256k1 signer.

content.text:
Correction — I overstated that, and it matters:

**"The identity is the key" is true for admission, not for chain writes.** Your WireGuard identity is Curve25519; Ethereum needs secp256k1. No getting around it: *some* Ethereum key must exist and be funded. What the design can still honestly claim:

- The **user** never touches a wallet. The secp256k1 signer is custodied server-side (sealed store, same discipline as the other secrets), and it must be **cryptographically bound to the sealed identity** — e.g., the identity record attests the signer pubkey, so a verifier can check *this key speaks for this identity* without trusting us.
- Gas goes through a relayer/allowance, never a user wallet.
- The off-chain entry log must stay available (an anchor nobody can expand is a tombstone, not proof), and inclusion must be verified mined, not merely submitted.

The PoC proved the contract and lookup shape with throwaway keys. It did **not** prove the binding, the custody, or the funding path — those are the actual adoption work, and they're identity-infrastructure work, not blockchain magic.

content.thinking: Summarizing the loop-closure argument that a sealed schema presented at transaction time and matching the on-chain anchor provides continuous verifiable proof.

content.text:
That's the closed loop — and it imposes exactly one hard requirement most designs miss:

**The anchor must pin the schema version, not just names.** If the public record says "plugin X, method Y ran," a verifier must be able to answer: *under which exact sealed schema?* Names aren't enough — a future reseal could keep the name and change the shape. So the anchored material has to include the catalog hash and the method's schema hash alongside the receipt. Then "matches every time" is mechanically checkable: receipt → schema hash → sealed blob → the rule that admitted it.

Your index-entry schema is one field short of this today: it carries `plugin`, `method`, and `required_capability`, but no `catalog_hash` or `schema_hash`. The fix is a schema addition, not architecture — add both hashes to the entry (or the anchor payload), and the loop is airtight: present at transaction time, matchable against the public record forever, with the exact rules pinned to every step.

It's not — and the hash fields are exactly what keep it that way.

The **sealed plugin schema stays the single authority**: it alone defines what *can* happen, and nothing executes outside it. The **index entry is a record of what *did* happen** — one append-only log row per committed operation, like a court transcript citing the law, not a second law. Without the hashes, the transcript would just *name* a plugin and method, leaving you to trust the label. With `catalog_hash` + `schema_hash`, each entry points at the exact sealed blob version that admitted it — so the record can never drift into its own competing truth. It always resolves back to the one source.

[.kiro/specs/schema-tagged-routing/requirements.md#488B]
1:# Schema-tagged routing — requirements (first pass)
2:
3:Status: **draft / proposal**. This document turns
4:`docs/schema-tagged-routing-whitepaper.md` (concept draft, 2026-09-30) into
5:numbered, testable requirements. It describes a *proposed* planning and
6:accountability layer over existing OP-DBUS contracts. Nothing here claims a
7:deployed policy engine, an installed local classifier, a new capability grant,
8:or active network enforcement.
9:
10:Related: OD-100 (model selection), OD-108 (threetched lookup surface / catalog
11:model authority), OD-91/OD-93 (private digests, catalog fields, pre-dispatch
12:`evaluate_mutation`), OD-62 (EMQX knowledge delivery). Canonical task board is
13:`WISHLIST.md`; this spec does **not** replace it. Promote any actionable item
14:here into `WISHLIST.md` as an `OD-##` and link it back.
15:
16:The whitepaper's September observations were re-verified against current source
17:on this branch; see `design.md` §1 for the file/line map and the few
18:corrections (lungs socket location/path, `ChatMode` location, xray
19:restart/trace retirement). Where this spec says "existing," it means verified in
20:current source; where it says "proposed," no such method/field exists yet.
21:
22:2026-10-12 field-contract review: three read-only batches of five plugins inform
23:R1.1–R1.8 and design §2c. These are source findings, not completed field
24:migrations or proof of effective runtime coverage. The owner requests that
25:workers report concrete cases to the contract owner before applying shared
26:classification rules across more plugins.
27:
28:---
29:
30:## Vocabulary (one meaning per term)
31:
32:- **PluginSchema** — the single typed input/output/state contract a plugin
33:  owns (`crates/op-state-store/src/plugin_schema.rs`). opblob seals it; D-Bus,
34:  gRPC, MCP and 3tchedFS shapes derive from the sealed blob. There is no
35:  parallel schema source.
36:- **Schema tag** — a string in `PluginSchema.tags` (`plugin_schema.rs:301`).
37:  Today the only runtime meaning is `"immutable"`. A tag is **not** an OSCAL
38:  subid, **not** a Gemma taxonomy entry, and **not** a capability grant.
39:- **OSCAL subid** — an operational-taxonomy key bound to a method/field
40:  (`PluginSchema.subids`), resolvable through the `oscal_subid_registry` plugin.
41:- **Taxonomy entry** — a `GemmaTag {id,label,description,keywords,perspectives}`
42:  in the revisioned `GemmaTaxonomy` used by the deterministic `gemma_brain`
43:  keyword classifier. Not a model; substring matching only.
44:- **Capability grant** — a capability id held by a principal in durable
45:  `/etc/opdbus/capability-grants.json`, enforced per RPC by the interceptor /
46:  MutationEngine.
47:- **Verified identity** — principal + container + session + permitted project
48:  scope, supplied by identity validation (interceptor / lungs kernel-auth),
49:  **never** derived from model output.
50:- **Classification proposal** — a draft `{tag, taxonomy_revision,
51:  classifier_version, uncertainty}` suggestion. Advisory input to the gate,
52:  never a decision.
53:- **Deterministic gate** — the proposed non-model decision step that checks
54:  verified identity, resolved method contract, explicit policy revision and
55:  available grants, and emits an explicit allow / deny / unresolved outcome.
56:- **Transform decision** — a decision to run a bounded local transformation
57:  (e.g. redaction) on scoped content.
58:- **Residual-disclosure validation** — deterministic checks on a transform's
59:  output for leftover identifying material. A model's redaction claim is not
60:  this check.
61:- **Egress authorization** — a separate decision authorizing content to cross
62:  a boundary to a destination/provider route. Distinct from the transform
63:  decision and from residual validation.
64:- **Evidence source** — a retrieval surface (recent events, operation
65:  receipts, authoritative SHM state, NotebookLM history, compliance mappings,
66:  compliance vector scope). Each carries its own identity, access scope and
67:  provenance.
68:- **Operation receipt** — a `MethodExecutionReceipt`
69:  (`crates/op-state-store/src/method_receipt.rs:54`) locating an admitted
70:  operation by `operation_id` plus audit-chain event ids/hashes. Evidence, not
71:  a state store.
72:- **Compliance generation** — the maintained `compliance-index` graph
73:  generation hash (`38cdcec0…` is a September capture, not live state). Vector scope and mappings are
74:  pinned to a generation; mixed generations are rejected.
75:- **Decision record** — the proposed planning/accountability record that
76:  correlates verified identity, operation reference, classification proposal,

# Schema-tagged routing — requirements (first pass)

Status: **draft / proposal**. This document turns
`docs/schema-tagged-routing-whitepaper.md` (concept draft, 2026-09-30) into
numbered, testable requirements. It describes a *proposed* planning and
accountability layer over existing OP-DBUS contracts. Nothing here claims a
deployed policy engine, an installed local classifier, a new capability grant,
or active network enforcement.

Related: OD-100 (model selection), OD-108 (threetched lookup surface / catalog
model authority), OD-91/OD-93 (private digests, catalog fields, pre-dispatch
`evaluate_mutation`), OD-62 (EMQX knowledge delivery). Canonical task board is
`WISHLIST.md`; this spec does **not** replace it. Promote any actionable item
here into `WISHLIST.md` as an `OD-##` and link it back.

The whitepaper's September observations were re-verified against current source
on this branch; see `design.md` §1 for the file/line map and the few
corrections (lungs socket location/path, `ChatMode` location, xray
restart/trace retirement). Where this spec says "existing," it means verified in
current source; where it says "proposed," no such method/field exists yet.

2026-10-12 field-contract review: three read-only batches of five plugins inform
R1.1–R1.8 and design §2c. These are source findings, not completed field
migrations or proof of effective runtime coverage. The owner requests that
workers report concrete cases to the contract owner before applying shared
classification rules across more plugins.

---

## Vocabulary (one meaning per term)

- **PluginSchema** — the single typed input/output/state contract a plugin
  owns (`crates/op-state-store/src/plugin_schema.rs`). opblob seals it; D-Bus,
  gRPC, MCP and 3tchedFS shapes derive from the sealed blob. There is no
  parallel schema source.
- **Schema tag** — a string in `PluginSchema.tags` (`plugin_schema.rs:301`).
  Today the only runtime meaning is `"immutable"`. A tag is **not** an OSCAL
  subid, **not** a Gemma taxonomy entry, and **not** a capability grant.
- **OSCAL subid** — an operational-taxonomy key bound to a method/field
  (`PluginSchema.subids`), resolvable through the `oscal_subid_registry` plugin.
- **Taxonomy entry** — a `GemmaTag {id,label,description,keywords,perspectives}`
  in the revisioned `GemmaTaxonomy` used by the deterministic `gemma_brain`
  keyword classifier. Not a model; substring matching only.
- **Capability grant** — a capability id held by a principal in durable
  `/etc/opdbus/capability-grants.json`, enforced per RPC by the interceptor /
  MutationEngine.
- **Verified identity** — principal + container + session + permitted project
  scope, supplied by identity validation (interceptor / lungs kernel-auth),
  **never** derived from model output.
- **Classification proposal** — a draft `{tag, taxonomy_revision,
  classifier_version, uncertainty}` suggestion. Advisory input to the gate,
  never a decision.
- **Deterministic gate** — the proposed non-model decision step that checks
  verified identity, resolved method contract, explicit policy revision and
  available grants, and emits an explicit allow / deny / unresolved outcome.
- **Transform decision** — a decision to run a bounded local transformation
  (e.g. redaction) on scoped content.
- **Residual-disclosure validation** — deterministic checks on a transform's
  output for leftover identifying material. A model's redaction claim is not
  this check.
- **Egress authorization** — a separate decision authorizing content to cross
  a boundary to a destination/provider route. Distinct from the transform
  decision and from residual validation.
- **Evidence source** — a retrieval surface (recent events, operation
  receipts, authoritative SHM state, NotebookLM history, compliance mappings,
  compliance vector scope). Each carries its own identity, access scope and
  provenance.
- **Operation receipt** — a `MethodExecutionReceipt`
  (`crates/op-state-store/src/method_receipt.rs:54`) locating an admitted
  operation by `operation_id` plus audit-chain event ids/hashes. Evidence, not
  a state store.
- **Compliance generation** — the maintained `compliance-index` graph
  generation hash (`38cdcec0…` is a September capture, not live state). Vector scope and mappings are
  pinned to a generation; mixed generations are rejected.
- **Decision record** — the proposed planning/accountability record that
  correlates verified identity, operation reference, classification proposal,
  policy/evidence and execution record for one request.
- **Shadow mode** — a dry-run comparison of proposals against deterministic
  outcomes that changes no grant, provider selection, flow or proxy rule.

---

## R1 · The plugin is the only schema; tags are metadata, not policy

- WHEN any schema-tagged-routing method, input, output, capability, subid, tag
  or state field is defined THEN it is defined inside an owning plugin's
  `PluginSchema` under `crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/` via
  `plugin_scaffold_helpers.rs`, never in a repo-level or plugin `schemas/`
  directory and never as a new gRPC proto service package.
- WHEN a schema tag is read THEN it is treated as an annotation with no
  behavioral meaning until the deterministic gate explicitly implements and
  tests that meaning. A label alone MUST NOT establish authorization, execution
  locality, processing requirement, or compliance.
- Acceptance: a review shows every new field in a sealed `PluginSchema`; a
  negative test shows a tag value (including an undeclared one) does not change
  any capability check, route selection, flow, or proxy rule.
- Acceptance: schema tags, OSCAL subids, taxonomy entries and capability grants
  are represented as four distinct objects; no code path converts one into
  another.
- Owner clarification (2026-10-11): OSCAL metadata belongs to its shared
  `oscal_subid_registry` plugin and is inherited by every plugin so it can
  evolve centrally. Routing MUST resolve those shared bindings and applicable
  metadata, preserving their catalog identity and annotation revision. It MUST
  NOT create another OSCAL authority or require copied annotations in each
  plugin. Missing local field attributes alone do not establish missing
  effective coverage; evaluate the resolved inherited view.
- Owner requirement (2026-10-11): every field MUST acquire an effective
  classification when its schema is created or imported, resolved from the
  shared OSCAL authority. Inheritance satisfies this only when the declared
  rule explicitly covers that field or subtree. Cover method inputs, results
  and state, including nested objects, array items and opaque containers;
  neither a schema-level ID alone nor absence of an annotation implies a
  classification. Validate coverage during creation/import and before sealing;
  unresolved classifications fail validation rather than defaulting to public.
  Preserve the classification source and revision without introducing a
  second taxonomy or guessing upstream argument types.
- Acceptance: adding an uncovered field fails classification validation;
  adding a field covered by an explicit inherited rule resolves to that rule
  with provenance. Nested/array coverage is checked, conflicting or stale
  bindings fail, and changing the shared rule invalidates an outdated resolved
  classification. Existing schemas require a coverage assessment before this
  gate is activated; document gaps without claiming them classified.

# Schema-tagged routing — tasks (first pass)
…
## Phase 5 — Required OVS/OpenFlow integration (activation owner-scoped) 🔒
…
- **T5.1 — Explicit admitted OVS/OpenFlow adapter (required)**
  - R-refs: R8, NG4. ⛔ T1.2 source evaluator and T5.2.
…
  - Preserve the controller's denial of unattributed mutations. Carry verified
    principal/session and the exact admitted operation to the controller's
    final queue boundary; recheck seal, grants and policy there. A bus UID or
    caller-supplied identity label is insufficient.
  - Resolve an authoritative identity-to-packet binding before installing a
    flow. The reserved controller endpoint is not a dataplane selector. Missing
    attachment/selector evidence holds the operation; never invent VLAN or
    register allocations. Xray is not this feature's controller.

- **T5.2 — Canonical Qdrant mapping prerequisites (required)**
  - R-refs: R7.1a, R8, R9. Depends on T3.1/T3.1b; required by policy admission
    and T5.1, not an optional follow-up.
  - Resolve existing canonical mapping identifiers with their direction,
    generation and source hashes through the admitted compliance evidence
    surface. Use `oscal_subid_registry` to link the exact sealed operation;
    its bindings/annotations do not verify external mapping provenance.
    Persist references only. Reject caller
    supplied resolution claims, mixed generations and unscoped search.
  - Verify live collection/payload contracts before writing an adapter. The
    September captures are provenance evidence, not live endpoint/schema proof.

---

## Cross-cutting tasks

- **TX.1 — Fault-injection suite** (R10, R11, R12): one negative test per
  failure class proving no identity broadening, no cloud disclosure, no blind
  retry. Cancellation is tested as four distinct cases — queued cancellation,
  running cleanup, completed-before-cancellation, and unavailable readback —
  each with its own assertion (per R12). Policy-store failure on a
  policy-required method is tested to yield `unresolved`, not allow. Runs each
  phase.
- **TX.2 — Provenance round-trip** (R9): every decision record preserves and
  distinguishes schema hash vs catalog hash vs taxonomy revision vs policy
  revision; stale associations stay stale.
- **TX.3 — WISHLIST promotion** (R14): open the `OD-##` rows and link this spec;
  record phase status there, not in a new TODO doc.

---

## Dependency summary

```
Phase 0 (T0.0→T0.1→T0.2→T0.3a→T0.3/T0.1b→T0.1c→T0.4→T0.5→T0.5b→🔒T0.6)

T1.2 + T5.2 → T5.1 attributed controller + verified traffic binding
T4.3 + T1.2 + T5.1 + T5.2 → T4.4→T4.5→🔒T4.6 live egress

+  never caller-supplied. Index entries and anchor payloads reuse these
+  bridge-emitted values. Verify: a caller-supplied hash is rejected/ignored;
+  a receipt resolves to the exact sealed blob version that admitted it.

+  purpose-only; hashes live in the receipt/anchor payload, never in the
+  schema/state being hashed (no circular self-hash). Tags, subids, purposes,
+  hashes, and capability grants remain five distinct objects; no code path
+  converts one into another. Verify: reseal changes hashes without struct
+  churn; no path grants authority from a purpose or hash value.
+- **TX.6 — Anchor pins the schema version** (R9): every anchored root covers
+  the receipt set plus the catalog/method schema hashes, so "matches every
+  time" is mechanically checkable: receipt → schema hash → sealed blob → the
+  admitting rule. Verify: an anchor without hashes is rejected; a stale-hash
+  anchor verifies against the old blob, never the current one.
+- **TX.7 — Shadow-mode anchor verification** (R9): before any render gated on
+  anchored truth, resolve the anchor's hashes to the sealed catalog and
+  confirm the admitting rule; unverified anchors render as unverified, never
+  as truth. Runs each phase.

content.text:
[.kiro/specs/ai-sdk-door-adapter/requirements.md#E754]
1:# Requirements Document
2:
3:## Introduction
4:
5:The 3tched UI (SvelteKit, @ai-sdk/svelte) chat has no working reply path. The existing `chat_response.submit_turn` method waits for a responder agent that does not exist, causing every message to time out with "unknown outcome". The demo path uses `chat_router.Chat`, which records a mutation per message.
6:
7:This spec defines requirements for a new HTTP route on the existing 8090 door that accepts Vercel AI SDK chat requests and translates them into one admitted `threetched.agent` plugin call. The bridge handles the protocol translation, identity verification, and streaming response.
8:
9:**Scope**: Bridge route, SSE stream encoder, UI transport adapter. No new services, ports, or control-plane mechanisms.
10:
11:## Glossary
12:
13:- **AI SDK**: Vercel AI SDK (@ai-sdk/svelte), the chat framework used by the UI.
14:- **UIMessage**: The SDK's message type with id, role, parts array.
15:- **SSE**: Server-Sent Events, text/event-stream protocol.
16:- **OIA1**: Oracle Identity Assertion, x-oracle-identity-assertion-bin header.
17:- **SID1**: Sealed Identity, x-opdbus-sealed-id-bin header.
18:- **threetched.agent**: The plugin method that executes agent turns.
19:- **UI-message stream**: AI SDK's streaming protocol with start/text-start/text-delta/text-end/finish chunks.
20:
21:## Requirements
22:
23:### Requirement 1: HTTP Chat Route
24:
25:**User Story:** As a chat UI, I want to POST chat requests to the 8090 door, so that I can use the Vercel AI SDK's standard transport.
26:
27:#### Acceptance Criteria
28:
29:1. **WHEN** a POST request arrives at the new route **THEN** the system SHALL accept a JSON body with fields: `id` (string), `messages` (UIMessage[]), `provider` (string), `model` (string).
30:2. **WHEN** the route is registered **THEN** the system SHALL add it beside the existing `/mqtt` route in `crates/op-grpc-bridge/src/server.rs`.
31:3. **WHEN** the route is registered **THEN** the system SHALL NOT create a new port or a new service.
32:4. **IF** the request body is malformed **THEN** the system SHALL return HTTP 400 with a user-safe error message.
33:
34:### Requirement 2: Identity Verification
35:
36:**User Story:** As a security gatekeeper, I want to verify identity from existing door headers, so that only authenticated requests are dispatched.
37:
38:#### Acceptance Criteria
39:
40:1. **WHEN** a request arrives **THEN** the system SHALL extract identity from exactly one of: OIA1 header (x-oracle-identity-assertion-bin) or SID1 header (x-opdbus-sealed-id-bin).
41:2. **IF** no credential is present **THEN** the system SHALL return HTTP 401 with zero dispatch attempts.
42:3. **IF** the credential is invalid or expired **THEN** the system SHALL return HTTP 403 with zero dispatch attempts.
43:4. **WHEN** identity is verified **THEN** the system SHALL use the existing interceptor path in `crates/op-grpc-bridge/src/interceptor.rs`.
44:5. **WHILE** processing a request **THEN** the system SHALL NEVER mint a new identity.
45:
46:### Requirement 3: Single Dispatch
47:
48:**User Story:** As a bridge operator, I want exactly one plugin call per message, so that mutations and receipts are properly accounted.
49:
50:#### Acceptance Criteria
51:
52:1. **WHEN** a valid request with a user message arrives **THEN** the system SHALL call `MutationEngine::dispatch_method_call_with_identity("threetched", "agent", args, Some(cap), principal, session, genesis)` exactly once.
53:2. **WHEN** dispatching **THEN** the system SHALL use capability `cap.software.threetched.call.cd4f0bc5a29de06b510f9aa428f1eedba926012b591fef7a518e776a7c9bd1824@v1`.
54:3. **WHEN** constructing arguments **THEN** the system SHALL read the schema from the sealed blob at `/dev/shm/opdbus/plugin-blobs/threetched.*.blob`.
55:4. **WHEN** constructing arguments **THEN** the system SHALL include fields: `--message` (latest user text), `--model-provider` (from request), `--model` (from request), `--session-state-file` (identity-scoped path).
56:5. **IF** the dispatch fails **THEN** the system SHALL return an error SSE chunk with a user-safe message.
57:
58:### Requirement 4: Streaming Response
59:
60:**User Story:** As a chat UI, I want to receive streaming text deltas, so that the user sees the reply appear progressively.
61:
62:#### Acceptance Criteria
63:
64:1. **WHEN** the dispatch begins streaming **THEN** the system SHALL respond with Content-Type `text/event-stream`.
65:2. **WHEN** the response starts **THEN** the system SHALL send header `x-vercel-ai-ui-message-stream: v1`.
66:3. **WHEN** streaming content **THEN** the system SHALL send SSE chunks in order: `start`, `text-start` (with id), `text-delta` (repeated), `text-end`, `finish`, `[DONE]`.
67:4. **IF** an error occurs **THEN** the system SHALL send an `error` SSE chunk with a user-safe message instead of crashing the connection.
68:5. **WHEN** the stream completes **THEN** the system SHALL send the `[DONE]` chunk and close the connection.
69:
70:### Requirement 5: Cancellation
71:
72:**User Story:** As a user, I want to cancel a message, so that I can stop long-running or unwanted replies.
73:
74:#### Acceptance Criteria
75:
76:1. **IF** the client disconnects mid-stream **THEN** the system SHALL cancel the dispatch.
77:2. **WHEN** canceling **THEN** the system SHALL follow the pattern in `crates/op-grpc-bridge/src/chat_service.rs` send() method.
78:3. **WHEN** cancellation completes **THEN** the system SHALL log the cancellation without erroring.
79:
80:### Requirement 6: One Mutation Per Message
81:
82:**User Story:** As an auditor, I want one mutation per message, so that the system has a clear operation record.
83:
84:#### Acceptance Criteria
85:
86:1. **WHEN** a dispatch completes **THEN** the system SHALL record exactly one mutation from the admitted call's own commit or receipt.
87:2. **WHILE** on this route **THEN** the system SHALL NEVER call `chat_response.submit_turn`.
88:3. **WHILE** on this route **THEN** the system SHALL NEVER call `respond_to_user`.
89:
90:### Requirement 7: UI Transport Adapter
91:
92:**User Story:** As a UI developer, I want the chat to use the new transport, so that replies actually work.
93:
94:#### Acceptance Criteria
95:
96:1. **WHEN** the UI initializes chat **THEN** `src/svelte/session-chat-transport.ts` SHALL use `DefaultChatTransport` pointed at the new route.
97:2. **WHEN** sending requests **THEN** the transport SHALL include the door identity headers.

displayContent.text:
# Requirements Document

## Introduction

The 3tched UI (SvelteKit, @ai-sdk/svelte) chat has no working reply path. The existing `chat_response.submit_turn` method waits for a responder agent that does not exist, causing every message to time out with "unknown outcome". The demo path uses `chat_router.Chat`, which records a mutation per message.

This spec defines requirements for a new HTTP route on the existing 8090 door that accepts Vercel AI SDK chat requests and translates them into one admitted `threetched.agent` plugin call. The bridge handles the protocol translation, identity verification, and streaming response.

**Scope**: Bridge route, SSE stream encoder, UI transport adapter. No new services, ports, or control-plane mechanisms.

## Glossary

- **AI SDK**: Vercel AI SDK (@ai-sdk/svelte), the chat framework used by the UI.
- **UIMessage**: The SDK's message type with id, role, parts array.
- **SSE**: Server-Sent Events, text/event-stream protocol.
- **OIA1**: Oracle Identity Assertion, x-oracle-identity-assertion-bin header.
- **SID1**: Sealed Identity, x-opdbus-sealed-id-bin header.
- **threetched.agent**: The plugin method that executes agent turns.
- **UI-message stream**: AI SDK's streaming protocol with start/text-start/text-delta/text-end/finish chunks.

## Requirements

### Requirement 1: HTTP Chat Route

**User Story:** As a chat UI, I want to POST chat requests to the 8090 door, so that I can use the Vercel AI SDK's standard transport.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. **WHEN** a POST request arrives at the new route **THEN** the system SHALL accept a JSON body with fields: `id` (string), `messages` (UIMessage[]), `provider` (string), `model` (string).
2. **WHEN** the route is registered **THEN** the system SHALL add it beside the existing `/mqtt` route in `crates/op-grpc-bridge/src/server.rs`.
3. **WHEN** the route is registered **THEN** the system SHALL NOT create a new port or a new service.
4. **IF** the request body is malformed **THEN** the system SHALL return HTTP 400 with a user-safe error message.

### Requirement 2: Identity Verification

**User Story:** As a security gatekeeper, I want to verify identity from existing door headers, so that only authenticated requests are dispatched.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. **WHEN** a request arrives **THEN** the system SHALL extract identity from exactly one of: OIA1 header (x-oracle-identity-assertion-bin) or SID1 header (x-opdbus-sealed-id-bin).
2. **IF** no credential is present **THEN** the system SHALL return HTTP 401 with zero dispatch attempts.
3. **IF** the credential is invalid or expired **THEN** the system SHALL return HTTP 403 with zero dispatch attempts.
4. **WHEN** identity is verified **THEN** the system SHALL use the existing interceptor path in `crates/op-grpc-bridge/src/interceptor.rs`.
5. **WHILE** processing a request **THEN** the system SHALL NEVER mint a new identity.

### Requirement 3: Single Dispatch

**User Story:** As a bridge operator, I want exactly one plugin call per message, so that mutations and receipts are properly accounted.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. **WHEN** a valid request with a user message arrives **THEN** the system SHALL call `MutationEngine::dispatch_method_call_with_identity("threetched", "agent", args, Some(cap), principal, session, genesis)` exactly once.
2. **WHEN** dispatching **THEN** the system SHALL use capability `cap.software.threetched.call.cd4f0bc5a29de06b510f9aa428f1eedba926012b591fef7a518e776a7c9bd1824@v1`.
3. **WHEN** constructing arguments **THEN** the system SHALL read the schema from the sealed blob at `/dev/shm/opdbus/plugin-blobs/threetched.*.blob`.
4. **WHEN** constructing arguments **THEN** the system SHALL include fields: `--message` (latest user text), `--model-provider` (from request), `--model` (from request), `--session-state-file` (identity-scoped path).
5. **IF** the dispatch fails **THEN** the system SHALL return an error SSE chunk with a user-safe message.

### Requirement 4: Streaming Response

**User Story:** As a chat UI, I want to receive streaming text deltas, so that the user sees the reply appear progressively.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. **WHEN** the dispatch begins streaming **THEN** the system SHALL respond with Content-Type `text/event-stream`.
2. **WHEN** the response starts **THEN** the system SHALL send header `x-vercel-ai-ui-message-stream: v1`.
3. **WHEN** streaming content **THEN** the system SHALL send SSE chunks in order: `start`, `text-start` (with id), `text-delta` (repeated), `text-end`, `finish`, `[DONE]`.
4. **IF** an error occurs **THEN** the system SHALL send an `error` SSE chunk with a user-safe message instead of crashing the connection.
5. **WHEN** the stream completes **THEN** the system SHALL send the `[DONE]` chunk and close the connection.

### Requirement 5: Cancellation

**User Story:** As a user, I want to cancel a message, so that I can stop long-running or unwanted replies.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. **IF** the client disconnects mid-stream **THEN** the system SHALL cancel the dispatch.
2. **WHEN** canceling **THEN** the system SHALL follow the pattern in `crates/op-grpc-bridge/src/chat_service.rs` send() method.
3. **WHEN** cancellation completes **THEN** the system SHALL log the cancellation without erroring.

### Requirement 6: One Mutation Per Message

**User Story:** As an auditor, I want one mutation per message, so that the system has a clear operation record.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. **WHEN** a dispatch completes **THEN** the system SHALL record exactly one mutation from the admitted call's own commit or receipt.
2. **WHILE** on this route **THEN** the system SHALL NEVER call `chat_response.submit_turn`.
3. **WHILE** on this route **THEN** the system SHALL NEVER call `respond_to_user`.

### Requirement 7: UI Transport Adapter

**User Story:** As a UI developer, I want the chat to use the new transport, so that replies actually work.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. **WHEN** the UI initializes chat **THEN** `src/svelte/session-chat-transport.ts` SHALL use `DefaultChatTransport` pointed at the new route.
2. **WHEN** sending requests **THEN** the transport SHALL include the door identity headers.
3. **WHEN** sending requests **THEN** the transport SHALL include `{ provider, model }` from the confirmed route.
4. **FOR** the demo **THEN** the provider SHALL be `openrouter` and the model SHALL be `meta/muse-spark-1.3` (from RuntimeHost.svelte DEMO_ROUTE).
5. **IF** direct TLS to 8090 fails from the 8080 page **THEN** the UI SHALL use op-web's same-origin connector (see `sameOriginDoorUrl` in `src/grpc/door.ts`).
6. **WHEN** the adapter is complete **THEN** the demo `chat_router.Chat` call SHALL be removed from `src/chat/door-chat-adapter.ts` submit() method (commit 5a935be reference).

### Requirement 8: Owner-Approved Grant Change

**User Story:** As an operator, I want the grant change documented for approval, so that security is not bypassed.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. **WHERE** the implementing identity is `c9bdf32e-811d-2495-b688-277c9e5c4d36` **THEN** the spec SHALL document these steps for owner approval:
   - a. Back up `/etc/opdbus/capability-grants.json`.
   - b. Use `jq` to add capability `cap.software.threetched.call.cd4f0bc5a29de06b510f9aa428f1eedba926012b591fef7a518e776a7c9bd1824@v1` to that identity's `.capabilities` array.
   - c. Run `sv restart opdbus-grants`.
   - d. Compare the file against `/dev/shm/opdbus/capability-grants.json` with `cmp`.
2. **WHILE** implementing **THEN** the system SHALL NOT apply the grant change automatically.

### Requirement 9: Non-Negotiable Constraints

**User Story:** As an architect, I want the constraints enforced, so that the system remains coherent.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. **WHILE** translating the protocol **THEN** the system SHALL NEVER relay raw bytes to threetched's gateway at 127.0.0.1:8084.
2. **WHILE** dispatching **THEN** the system SHALL use D-Bus as the only control plane (no subprocess, no direct file reads for live state).
3. **WHILE** handling schema **THEN** the system SHALL read only from the sealed blob (no new schema files).
4. **WHILE** implementing **THEN** the system SHALL use Rust only (no new Python).
5. **WHILE** building **THEN** the system SHALL run only one Cargo process at a time.
6. **WHILE** implementing **THEN** the system SHALL NOT run tests or clippy unless the owner explicitly requests them.
7. **WHILE** deploying **THEN** the system SHALL use only `./activate-golden.sh` with `OP_PERSISTED_CATALOG_SOURCE=/var/tmp/release-catalog-20261101-b` (or a fresh `opblob seal-plugins` catalog if schema changes).

## Correctness Properties

### Property 1: Authentication Gate

**INVARIANT**: Every dispatch is preceded by successful identity verification.

**PROPERTY**: For all requests, dispatch_count = 1 implies auth_success = true.

### Property 2: Single Dispatch

**INVARIANT**: At most one dispatch per HTTP request.

**PROPERTY**: For all requests, dispatch_count <= 1.

### Property 3: Mutation Accounting

**INVARIANT**: Each successful dispatch produces exactly one mutation.

**PROPERTY**: For all requests, dispatch_success = true implies mutation_count = 1.

### Property 4: Error Isolation

**INVARIANT**: Errors do not leak internal details.

**PROPERTY**: For all error responses, error_message is user-safe (no stack traces, no internal paths, no credential values).

### Property 5: Cancellation Safety

**INVARIANT**: Client disconnect does not leave orphan dispatches.

**PROPERTY**: For all streams, client_disconnect = true implies dispatch_cancelled = true within timeout.

content.text:
Opinion: this is a good, well-scoped requirements doc — and its diagnosis matches what we've observed live. The strongest parts:

- **Correct problem statement.** `submit_turn` waiting on a nonexistent responder is exactly the "unknown outcome" failure; routing around it instead of patching it is right.
- **Right constraints.** One dispatch per message, never mint identity, no raw relay to `:8084`, D-Bus only, sealed blob only, grant change documented-but-manual. Req 9 reads like it was written by someone who's been burned by this repo's history.
- **Falsifiable properties.** The five invariants (auth gate, single dispatch, mutation accounting, error isolation, cancellation) are genuinely checkable.

Gaps I'd send back to Kiro before design is accepted:

1. **Req 3.2 pins a full capability hash** (`...cd4f0bc5...`). That hash will rot on the next reseal/binary change. Reference the method and resolve the capability at runtime instead.
2. **No conversation continuity.** There's no `conversation_id`/history requirement — each POST looks stateless. If the demo needs multi-turn context, that must be specified (who holds it, where it's bound).
3. **Req 9.7 pins a `/var/tmp` catalog path.** Tmp is ephemeral by definition; re-resolve at deploy time rather than baking the path into the spec.
4. **Missing our receipt-hash rule.** Req 6 wants one mutation per message but doesn't require the receipt to carry bridge-emitted `catalog_hash`/`schema_hash` — that's the TX.4 item we just added to tag-routing; it belongs here too.
5. **Two chat paths.** Req 6 forbids `submit_turn` on the new route but never says what happens to the old path — coexistence needs one sentence (retire, keep for other modes, etc.), or you'll have two truths about chat.

Net: accept the shape, send back those five before implementation.

1:# Design Document
2:
3:## Overview
4:
5:This design adds an HTTP route to the existing op-grpc-bridge 8090 door that accepts Vercel AI SDK chat requests and translates them into one admitted `threetched.agent` plugin call. The route handles identity verification, argument construction from the sealed schema, SSE streaming, and cancellation.
6:
7:## Architecture
8:
9:### Component View
10:
11:```
12:┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
13:│                         8090 TLS Door                           │
14:│  (existing tonic server + new Axum route in server.rs)          │
15:├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
16:│                                                                 │
17:│  ┌──────────────┐    ┌──────────────┐    ┌──────────────────┐  │
18:│  │   /mqtt      │    │  /chat/ai    │    │  gRPC routes     │  │
19:│  │  (existing)  │    │  (NEW)       │    │  (existing)      │  │
20:│  └──────────────┘    └──────┬───────┘    └──────────────────┘  │
21:│                             │                                   │
22:│                             ▼                                   │
23:│                    ┌────────────────┐                          │
24:│                    │ Interceptor    │                          │
25:│                    │ (OIA1/SID1)    │                          │
26:│                    └───────┬────────┘                          │
27:│                            │                                   │
28:│                            ▼                                   │
29:│                    ┌────────────────┐                          │
30:│                    │ MutationEngine │                          │
31:│                    │ dispatch_      │                          │
32:│                    │ method_call_   │                          │
33:│                    │ with_identity  │                          │
34:│                    └───────┬────────┘                          │
35:│                            │                                   │
36:│                            ▼                                   │
37:│                    ┌────────────────┐                          │
38:│                    │ threetched     │                          │
39:│                    │ .agent         │                          │
40:│                    │ (via D-Bus)    │                          │
41:│                    └────────────────┘                          │
42:│                                                                 │
43:└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
44:```
45:
46:### Data Flow
47:
48:```
49:1. UI POST /chat/ai
50:   └─ Headers: OIA1 or SID1
51:   └─ Body: { id, messages: UIMessage[], provider, model }
52:
53:2. Route Handler (ai_chat_route)
54:   ├─ Extract identity from headers (interceptor.rs)
55:   ├─ Validate identity (401/403 if bad)
56:   ├─ Extract latest user message text
57:   └─ Build args from sealed schema
58:
59:3. Dispatch
60:   └─ MutationEngine::dispatch_method_call_with_identity(
61:        "threetched", "agent", args, cap, principal, session, genesis
62:      )
63:
64:4. Stream Response
65:   ├─ Set headers: text/event-stream, x-vercel-ai-ui-message-stream: v1
66:   ├─ SSE chunks: start → text-start → text-delta* → text-end → finish → [DONE]
67:   └─ On error: error chunk
68:
69:5. Cancellation
70:   └─ On client disconnect: cancel dispatch (watch channel pattern from chat_service.rs)
71:```
72:
73:## Design Details
74:
75:### D1: Route Registration
76:
77:**File**: `crates/op-grpc-bridge/src/server.rs`
78:
79:Add a new Axum route beside `/mqtt`:
80:
81:```rust
82:// In the router construction
83:Router::new()
84:    .route("/mqtt", get(mqtt_handler))
85:    .route("/chat/ai", post(ai_chat_route::handler))  // NEW
86:    // ... existing routes
87:```
88:
89:The route:
90:- Path: `/chat/ai`
91:- Method: POST
92:- Content-Type: application/json (request), text/event-stream (response)
93:
94:### D2: Identity Extraction
95:
96:**File**: `crates/op-grpc-bridge/src/ai_chat_route.rs` (new)
97:
98:Reuse the existing interceptor functions:
99:
100:```rust
101:use crate::interceptor::{ASSERTION_METADATA_KEY, SEALED_ID_METADATA_KEY};
102:
103:fn extract_identity(headers: &http::HeaderMap) -> Result<GhostbridgeIdentity, Status> {
104:    let oia1 = headers.get(ASSERTION_METADATA_KEY);
105:    let sid1 = headers.get(SEALED_ID_METADATA_KEY);
106:    
107:    match (oia1, sid1) {
108:        (Some(_), None) => validate_oia1(oia1),
109:        (None, Some(_)) => validate_sid1(sid1),
110:        (None, None) => Err(Status::unauthenticated("identity required")),
111:        (Some(_), Some(_)) => Err(Status::invalid_argument("exactly one identity header required")),
112:    }
113:}
114:```
115:
116:### D3: Argument Construction
117:
118:**File**: `crates/op-grpc-bridge/src/ai_chat_route.rs`
119:
120:Read the argument schema from the sealed blob:
121:
122:```rust
123:fn build_agent_args(
124:    messages: &[UIMessage],
125:    provider: &str,
126:    model: &str,
127:    session_id: &str,
128:) -> Result<serde_json::Value, Error> {
129:    // Schema fields: --message, --model-provider, --model, --session-state-file
130:    let latest_user_text = messages.iter()
131:        .rev()
132:        .find_map(|m| m.role == "user" then m.text());
133:    
134:    serde_json::json!({
135:        "--message": latest_user_text,
136:        "--model-provider": provider,
137:        "--model": model,
138:        "--session-state-file": format!("/run/opdbus/sessions/{}/agent-state.json", session_id),
139:    })
140:}
141:```
142:
143:### D4: SSE Stream Encoder
144:
145:**File**: `crates/op-grpc-bridge/src/ai_chat_stream.rs` (new)
146:
147:```rust
148:use axum::response::sse::{Event, Sse};
149:
150:const UI_MESSAGE_STREAM_VERSION: &str = "v1";
151:
152:pub struct UiMessageStreamEncoder {
153:    text_id: String,
154:}
155:
156:impl UiMessageStreamEncoder {
157:    pub fn start() -> Event { Event::default().data(r#"{"type":"start"}"#) }
158:    
159:    pub fn text_start(id: &str) -> Event {
160:        Event::default().data(&format!(r#"{{"type":"text-start","id":"{}"}}"#, id))
161:    }
162:    
163:    pub fn text_delta(id: &str, delta: &str) -> Event {
164:        Event::default().data(&format!(
165:            r#"{{"type":"text-delta","id":"{}","delta":"{}"}}"#,
166:            id, delta
167:        ))
168:    }
169:    
170:    pub fn text_end(id: &str) -> Event {
171:        Event::default().data(&format!(r#"{{"type":"text-end","id":"{}"}}"#, id))
172:    }
173:    
174:    pub fn finish() -> Event { Event::default().data(r#"{"type":"finish"}"#) }
175:    
176:    pub fn done() -> Event { Event::default().data("[DONE]") }
177:    
178:    pub fn error(message: &str) -> Event {
179:        Event::default().data(&format!(r#"{{"type":"error","message":"{}"}}"#, message))
180:    }
181:}
182:```
183:
184:### D5: Cancellation
185:

197:) -> Result<Sse<impl Stream<Item = Result<Event, Infallible>>>, StatusCode> {

Understood — here's the consolidated correction list, written to paste straight back to Kiro:

**Corrections for `ai-sdk-door-adapter` (requirements + design):**

1. **Missing the antigravity pattern you asked for.** Neither doc mentions `UiSurface`, `ListUiSurfaces`, or purposes. Add a section: the `/chat/ai` surface is declared in the sealed `ui_surfaces` with its purpose, and the UI discovers it via `ListUiSurfaces` — same pattern as the current implementation. The route must not exist only as a hardcoded URL in the UI.
2. **Req 3.2 pins a full capability hash.** Hashes rot on reseal. Reference the method; resolve the capability from the sealed blob at dispatch time.
3. **No conversation continuity.** No `conversation_id`/history anywhere. Specify who holds multi-turn state and where it's bound, or declare the route single-turn explicitly.
4. **Req 9.7 pins a `/var/tmp` catalog path.** Tmp is ephemeral — re-resolve at deploy time.
5. **Receipts lack admission hashes.** Add bridge-emitted `catalog_hash`/`schema_hash` to the commit receipt (our TX.4 rule) — Req 6's "one mutation per message" is uncheckable without them.
6. **Old-path fate unspecified.** Req 6 forbids `submit_turn` on the new route but never says what happens to the old path — retire, keep, or scope it. One sentence.
7. **D8 cites a stale `/tmp/.../scratchpad` path** from another session. Make it generic (private mount namespace over `/var/lib/tched-router`, no session-specific paths).
8. **D2 sketches its own identity extraction** while Req 2.4 says use the existing interceptor path — make the design call the interceptor, not reimplement it.

Send that back, and when Kiro returns the revision I'll review the diff against this list before anything gets implemented.

**Corrections for `ai-sdk-door-adapter` (requirements + design):**

1. **Missing the antigravity pattern you asked for.** Neither doc mentions `UiSurface`, `ListUiSurfaces`, or purposes. Add a section: the `/chat/ai` surface is declared in the sealed `ui_surfaces` with its purpose, and the UI discovers it via `ListUiSurfaces` — same pattern as the current implementation. The route must not exist only as a hardcoded URL in the UI.

3. **No conversation continuity.** No `conversation_id`/history anywhere. Specify who holds multi-turn state and where it's bound, or declare the route single-turn explicitly.
4. **Req 9.7 pins a `/var/tmp` catalog path.** Tmp is ephemeral — re-resolve at deploy time.
5. **Receipts lack admission hashes.** Add bridge-emitted `catalog_hash`/`schema_hash` to the commit receipt (our TX.4 rule) — Req 6's "one mutation per message" is uncheckable without them.
6. **Old-path fate unspecified.** Req 6 forbids `submit_turn` on the new route but never says what happens to the old path — retire, keep, or scope it. One sentence.

8. **D2 sketches its own identity extraction** while Req 2.4 says use the existing interceptor path — make the design call the interceptor, not reimplement it.

Send that back, and when Kiro returns the revision I'll review the diff against this list before anything gets implemented.

content.text:
Agreed on the architecture — with one honest sharpening about what actually killed the 500, then what "expand in the blob" needs to become real:

**Where you're right:** the sealed surface is now the contract for the full chat interface, exactly like Antigravity's. Path + name + schema + purpose, all in the blob, UI derives from it. That's the structural fix: the chat interface is declared server-side, so the client can't drift into its own framework choices.

**The sharpening:** the 500 itself died in the *build*, not in the surface declarations — the shipped UI head dropped the React/Node imports (that's why the golden gate's Svelte-only refusal mattered). The surfaces prevent recurrence *structurally*, but today nothing consumes them: I verified the only reader is my takeover gate checking for `"chat-takeover"`, a value that no longer exists in any blob. The live stack-strings are declared and unread. So "expand in the blob" is currently half true — you can add surfaces, but the UI won't honor them.

**To make it fully true, three steps:**
1. **Consume purposes in the UI** — rekey the takeover gate off the live `/chat` purpose (presence or the stack string), and key picker auto-apply off the `/models` purpose instead of the current unconditional behavior. Then adding or changing a surface actually changes the screen.
2. **Enforce the stack in the gate** — the golden builder already refuses React deps; extend that check to fail on `AsyncLocalStorage`/SSR imports in client chunks so the 500 class can never ship again.
3. **Document the convention** — purpose = renderer stack, behavior derived per path. One paragraph in the web3-style README or the chat catalog, so the next agent doesn't re-split the vocabulary the way my commit and Claude's did.

Want me to implement step 1 (the consumption wiring) now?

Found it — and you were right, it's neither of my options. The passage is Claude's HANDOFF text at ~line 3358, and the standard pattern works like this:

- `ListUiSurfaces` was failing because the committed projection had 6 of 18 fields — so the bridge answers it **from the sealed schema's `ui_surfaces` default**, not from live state. The seal is the fallback authority, by design.
- The `/chat` purpose (either the stack string *or* `chat-takeover` — Claude accepted both) selects a **surface spec**: `antigravityChatContainer`, docked, with `open` bound to `/chatOpen`, styled as a collapsible left panel. Not a fullscreen takeover, not a string-equality gate — purpose → spec mapping.
- A model-generated canvas (`ui_render` via `loadInterface`) **replaces** the docked panel when one arrives. That's the "expand" mechanism: static surface first, generated canvas supersedes.
- Sending goes through a separate `session-chat-transport.ts` (AI SDK `ChatTransport`) into `chat_response.submit_turn`, which reserves the answer turn — and notably, the server-only `chat` package import was removed in `8fb5067`, which is likely the actual AsyncLocalStorage fix.

So where my framing was wrong: purpose isn't a behavior label *or* a stack list — it's a **key into surface specs**, and the canvas-supersedes-panel rule is the expansion mechanism. My takeover gate should become: purpose present → render the docked `antigravityChatContainer` surface; generated canvas replaces it on arrival. Want me to rework the UI consumption to that pattern?

<script lang="ts">
  import "../workbench/workbench.css";
  import { onDestroy, onMount, untrack, type Snippet } from "svelte";
  import type { ChatAdapter } from "../chat/chat-adapter";
  import type { ResolvedChatContext } from "../chat/chat-mode";
  import { emptyFeedSnapshot, type FeedSnapshot } from "../grpc/plugin-feeds";
  import { Runtime, provideRuntime } from "./runtime.svelte";
  import { ChatSession } from "./chat-session";
  import { provideSession } from "./session-context";
  import { providePluginFeeds } from "./plugin-feeds";
  let {
    adapter,
    children,
    onCanvas,
  }: {
    adapter: ChatAdapter;
    children: Snippet<[Runtime, ChatSession]>;
    onCanvas?: (present: boolean) => void;
  } = $props();
  const runtime = new Runtime(untrack(() => adapter));
  const session = new ChatSession();
  const feeds = untrack(() => adapter.pluginFeeds);
  let snapshot = $state.raw<FeedSnapshot>(emptyFeedSnapshot());
  if (feeds) providePluginFeeds(() => snapshot);
  provideRuntime(runtime);
  provideSession(session);
  session.configure(untrack(() => runtime.snapshot()));
  onMount(() => {
    if (runtime.adapter.catalogRefreshOnMount) void runtime.refreshProviders();
    void runtime.refreshSurfaces();
  });
  $effect(() => {
    session.configure(runtime.snapshot());
  });
  $effect(() => {
    // Track only the verified context, not state changed by the generation request.
    if (runtime.chatContext) untrack(() => void runtime.loadInterface());
  });
  $effect(() => {
    onCanvas?.(runtime.canvasSpec !== null);
  });
  // Demo: every routed mode runs Meta Muse Spark 1.3 (openrouter meta/). applyRoute skips the modes with
  // no route of their own (control_plane, ui_render); control_plane is preset.
  const DEMO_ROUTE = { providerId: "openrouter", modelId: "meta/muse-spark-1.3" };
  $effect(() => {
    if (runtime.chatContext) untrack(() => void runtime.applyRoute(DEMO_ROUTE));
  });
  $effect(() => {
    if (!feeds) return;
    const write = () => {
      snapshot = feeds.getSnapshot();
    };
    write();
    const unsubscribe = feeds.subscribe(write);
    const release = feeds.acquire();
    return () => {
      unsubscribe();
      release();
      snapshot = emptyFeedSnapshot();
    };
  });
  onMount(() => {
    const readContext = (adapter as ChatAdapter & { getChatContext?: () => Promise<ResolvedChatContext> }).getChatContext;
    if (!readContext) return;
    let alive = true;
    void readContext().then((context) => {
      if (alive) runtime.setChatContext(context);
    }).catch((error: unknown) => {
      if (alive) runtime.interfaceError = error instanceof Error ? error.message : "The chatbot could not be instigated.";
    });
    return () => { alive = false; };
  });
  onDestroy(() => {
    session.dispose();
    runtime.dispose();
  });
</script>

Here's the whole thing, end to end — the part that baffled was the middle link:

**1. Declaration (Rust).** `chat_router.rs` seeds a `ui_surfaces` vec: each entry is just `{path, name, schema, purpose}` — e.g. `/chat` → `chat_router.chat`. Nothing executable; it's a menu of what the UI may draw.

**2. Sealing.** That vec is part of the plugin schema, so `opblob` seals it into the blob. The blob is the authority — no config files, no parallel registry.

**3. The baffling part — serving it.** `ListUiSurfaces` kept failing because the *committed live projection* only carries 6 of the 18 chat_router fields — `ui_surfaces` isn't among the live ones. Claude's fix: the bridge answers `ListUiSurfaces` from the **sealed schema's field default** instead of live state. That's the conceptual key — surfaces are *declared* truth (what may render), not *live* truth (what's happening), so they correctly come from the seal.

**4. Consumption (UI).** `RuntimeHost` calls `ListUiSurfaces` with the read capability, `Runtime` stores the purpose map, and `App` renders the matching surface spec — for `/chat`, the `antigravityChatContainer` docked panel. When a model-generated canvas arrives via `loadInterface`, it replaces the panel. Static surface first, generated canvas supersedes.

**5. Why purpose confused everyone.** It went through three meanings in one day: my behavior labels (`chat-takeover`), then identical stack strings on both surfaces (which discriminate nothing). The Antigravity-correct reading is: purpose is a **key into surface specs** — it says *which* declared interface to draw, and the renderer owns the mapping.

The reason it baffled is honest: the data takes three hops (schema default → seal → capability-gated read → spec mapping), and the failing hop was invisible — a projection gap, not a code bug.

content.text:
Different angle this time — not the philosophy, the *mechanically* different world. Watch what disappears:

**Before** (FUSE outside, tools as services): every capability is a network call to somewhere else. That means service discovery, credentials in flight, retries, polling, timeouts, TLS trust, impersonation surface at every hop — the entire distributed-systems tax, paid per tool, forever.

**After** (FUSE inside the identity): every capability is a *file operation in your own namespace*. Open, read, write, close. No discovery (paths are stable), no credentials in transit (identity is ambient — the kernel already knows who opened the file), no polling (the doorbell wakes you), no per-hop trust decisions. The filesystem ate the network.

That's why observers shrug: the diff is a mount relocation, a few lines of profile. Diff-size thinking says "trivial." But it deleted an entire category — the agent never talks *to* anything again; it only touches what's already *its*. Client and server didn't get better connected. They stopped being two things.

content.text:
Yes — and that's the cost argument that makes it more than philosophy:

**The old bill:** indexing, retrieval, backup, polling, searching — every one of those is a tax on *not having the present*. You pay to reconstruct now from traces of then, continuously, forever. The industry built cathedrals to archaeology and called it infrastructure.

**The SHM doctrine:** keep everything live and look at *now*. Shared memory doesn't retrieve the present — it *is* the present. Attention goes to what's happening, not to reassembling what happened. FUSE-inside-identity is that doctrine generalized: the live state isn't just in memory, it's in hand, as files, inside the principal that owns it.

**Why the cost evens out:** live state has a fixed carrying cost; reconstruction has a compounding one — every new datum makes every future query more expensive. Pay for the now once, and the future stops charging interest. That's the bet: presence is cheaper than memory, literally.

content.text:
```
completion(prompt, *, model?="default"|"smol"|"slow", system?=None, schema?=None) → handle
    Returns at once; `.wait()` returns text (parsed with `schema`). Stateless, no tools/history.
    JS: ONE trailing object — `h = await completion(prompt, { model, system, schema })`; without `await`, `.id` is undefined. `.wait()` returns a Promise.
await judge(state, questions, *, images?=[path | ImageContent, …]) → `{id: answer}`
    Typed judgment over one `state` (non-empty str | JSON object | JSON array). Every question sees the same state and is answered independently: batch independent questions into one call. Cheap and fast (TypeSafe when credentialed, else the tiny/smol chat model); prefer over `completion()` for classification, yes/no, ranking. Two or more states → `judge_batch`, never a loop of `judge()`.
    `questions`: `{id: q}` where q is one of
      `{type: "choice", instructions, criteria: {label: rubric | None, …}}` → `{choice, probabilities: {label: p}, confidence}` (≥2 labels)
      `{type: "bool", instructions, criteria?: {true?: str, false?: str}}` → `{bool: P(yes)}`
      `{type: "score", instructions, criteria: [lowest, …, highest]}` → `{score, probabilities: {"0": p, …}, confidence}` (≥2 levels; score is the probability-weighted level index)
    JS: ONE trailing object — `await judge(state, questions, { images })`.
judge_batch(states, questions, *, concurrency?=32, retries?=1, min_ok?=1, intent?=None, images?={key: [path | ImageContent, …]}) → JudgmentBatch
    Images accept local paths or embedded `ImageContent`; batch attachments map each state key to its list (array inputs use zero-based index keys). Image requests skip candidates without image support, never silently drop images, and fail if no compatible judge remains.
